verdict.rationale: The evidence shows only general access management: SSO, SCIM provisioning, email-domain auto-join and inviting collaborators. Target-app scoping of client SDK keys controls which configs are visible to an SDK, not who may change them. Nothing documents roles or permissions that restrict which users can modify which flags, or Console API tokens scoped to limit write access, so these are adjacent controls rather than the capability itself.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can restrict who can change which flags with roles, permissions, and scoped API tokens
